topic: Calibrated selector envelopes for lossy causal abstractions. Let C be a finite pre-treatment context and X a finite micro-action in the fiber of macro intervention h. Assume p(c)>0, aggregate implementation shares r(x)>0, and Bernoulli micro-interventional means mu(c,x) are identified, but joint deployment logs are unavailable. The macro implementation uses independent selector noise with unknown s(x|c), and gamma(c,x)=p(c)s(x|c) has margins p and r. Prove that the compatible macro mean set is exactly {sum gamma(c,x)mu(c,x): gamma has margins p,r}; construct one common finite response SCM and compatible residual projection realizing every gamma in this explicitly free-selector Definition-6 class. Compute endpoints by min/max-cost flow, prove point identification iff all alternating mu contrasts vanish on the effective support graph, and return endpoint SCM selector certificates. With fixed finite support and positive margins, derive joint directional derivatives and pointwise simultaneous numerical-delta inference when p,r,mu are estimated together and optimal faces may be nonunique. Explicitly exclude the stronger claim that all selectors preserve one fixed canonical Equation-11 L3 map. Consumer: the Béal-Latouche PDX precision-medicine analysis when a target deployment provides tumor-profile frequencies and aggregate drug shares but not their joint allocation; report whether superiority to its control remains uniform over the sharp interval. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A fresh derivation obtained the exact selector-mixture formula, a common Bernoulli-response SCM realizing every margin-compatible coupling through independent selector noise, a structural compatible-residual projection, endpoint attainment, and the effective-support alternating-cycle iff. For the equal-margin two-context witness it derived theta(t)=1/4+(6/5)t on 0<=t<=1/2, hence the sharp interval [1/4,17/20]. Both endpoints and a nonunique-face derivative check were recomputed numerically; 13,824 finite residual/intervention diagrams satisfied the structural compatibility identity. Destructive checks separated this free-selector Definition-6 class from the stronger fixed canonical Equation-11 L3 map, handled forced-zero support edges, and found no exact query collision. Generic transport optimization and estimated-cost directional inference are acknowledged supporting machinery. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Complete the conditional numerical-delta convergence proof for simultaneous pointwise endpoint inference when margins and micro-response means are jointly estimated and both primal and dual optimal faces are nonunique. EARLY KILL TEST: Encode both endpoint selectors in the two-context, three-action partial-projection model and verify every Definition-6 structural diagram, then compute the common baseline canonical Equation-11 selector; pivot if the intended class requires both endpoints to preserve that one fixed canonical L3 map. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/scm_lossy_selector_envelope.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one prove joint pointwise numerical-delta inference for the lower and upper selector-envelope endpoints when p, r, and mu are estimated together, the margin equations are redundant, and both primal and dual optimal faces may be nonunique?

source_refs.claim: Hong and Li establish numerical-delta inference for directionally differentiable maps under step-size conditions, including pointwise consistency and uniform results for certain convex Lipschitz maps.
source_refs.author: Han Hong and Jessie Li

source_refs.claim: Fang and Santos show that the ordinary bootstrap generally fails for merely directionally differentiable functionals and provide derivative-based resampling inference.
source_refs.author: Zheng Fang and Andres Santos

source_refs.claim: Voronin handles sharp LP bounds when all coefficients are estimated and solutions are multiple, but uses a debiased LP-value estimator rather than the paired plug-in numerical-delta procedure required here.
source_refs.author: Andrei Voronin

source_refs.claim: The authors establish resampling inference for directionally differentiable optimized value functions, chiefly when optimization changes through the objective rather than through jointly moving transport costs and feasible margins.
source_refs.author: Sergio Firpo, Antonio F. Galvao, and Thomas Parker

open_problems.why_unsolved: The selector endpoint map perturbs both the transport cost mu and the equality-constraint right-hand side (p,r). Feasible perturbations lie in a common-total-mass tangent space because one margin equation is redundant, while nonunique optimal faces make each directional derivative a secondary optimization over primal and dual optimizer sets. Hong–Li applies only after Hadamard directional differentiability, a compatible perturbation domain, and tuning-rate control are established. Voronin proves multiplicity-robust inference using a different debiased estimator, so it does not settle conditional convergence of the requested paired plug-in numerical-delta law.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem deriving the joint directional derivative of the endpoint vector as face-wise primal-dual programs and proving conditional consistency of a projected numerical-delta resampling law that yields pointwise simultaneous confidence intervals under a joint CLT for estimated p, r, and mu.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the closest inferential problem: sharp LP bounds with all coefficients sampled and optimizer multiplicity allowed.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Sharp causal bounds are LP values -> plug-in endpoint behavior is nonregular at changing optimal faces -> inference must remain valid when constraints, costs, and optimizer sets all move

method_exemplars.technique: Approximate a Hadamard directional derivative by finite differences evaluated at resampled local perturbations and prove conditional weak convergence under tuning-rate conditions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the requested computational device; the new work is verifying its hypotheses on the transport tangent space for the joint endpoint functional.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply the directional functional delta method and consistently estimate the directional derivative when ordinary bootstrap inference fails.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The endpoint vector becomes nonsmooth exactly at multiple optimal faces, matching their canonical nonregular setting.

method_exemplars.technique: Debias estimated LP values through penalized feasibility and establish root-n pointwise normal inference under solution multiplicity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the strongest direct comparator for determining whether paired numerical-delta inference supplies a distinct valid procedure.

open_problems.open_problem: When micro-interventional means mu(c,x) and separate target margins p(c) and r(x) are known but context-by-version deployment is not logged, is the sharp macro-intervention mean set the image of the transportation polytope under gamma -> sum gamma(c,x)mu(c,x), with every feasible gamma realizable inside one common finite response SCM using independent selector noise?

source_refs.claim: Béal and Latouche formulate precision-medicine effects with multiple treatment versions and use PDX data, but do not study deployments known only through separate profile and drug-share margins.
source_refs.author: Jonas Béal and Aurélien Latouche

source_refs.claim: The macro effect of a treatment with multiple versions depends on the distribution used to assign versions, with identification developed when that distribution is specified or observed.
source_refs.author: Tyler J. VanderWeele and Miguel A. Hernán

source_refs.claim: For variables held in datasets that cannot be linked, the authors use optimal transport to constructively characterize a sharp identified set and develop inference from its geometry.
source_refs.author: Xavier D'Haultfœuille, Christophe Gaillac, and Arnaud Maurel

source_refs.claim: COTA combines causal-abstraction constraints with multi-marginal optimal transport to learn abstraction maps, rather than bounding an intervention value over unknown selector couplings.
source_refs.author: Yorgos Felekis, Fabio Massimo Zennaro, Nicola Branchini, and Theodoros Damoulas
source_refs.venue: Conference on Causal Learning and Reasoning, PMLR 236

open_problems.why_unsolved: The multiple-versions literature makes the macro effect depend on a specified conditional version distribution, while data-combination work optimizes over unlinked joint laws without proving the intervention semantics required by a lossy causal abstraction. COTA uses transport to learn abstraction maps rather than proving that every margin-compatible selector coupling has a common-SCM realization. The missing first step is therefore a causal sharpness equivalence: fixed response variables and a compatible residual projection must work for the whole transport polytope while selector mechanisms, but not micro responses, vary.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp-identification theorem equating the compatible macro-mean set to a closed interval computed by min/max-cost flow, together with one finite Bernoulli-response SCM and explicit endpoint selector certificates realizing every feasible coupling.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation proceeds from molecularly tailored recommendations to multiple drug versions and clinically meaningful control comparisons, matching the destination application.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Molecular profiles induce heterogeneous drug recommendations -> each macro strategy contains multiple drug versions -> missing joint target allocation makes the strategy value an interval rather than a point

method_exemplars.technique: Use transport duality to replace an unavailable joint distribution by optimization over couplings of observed margins and prove sharpness constructively.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The selector envelope is likewise a linear functional of an unavailable joint law constrained by two observed margins.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode causal commutativity constraints inside an optimal-transport construction between model levels.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest method combining causal-abstraction semantics with transport, although the desired result replaces map learning by sharp partial identification and common-SCM attainment.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate sharp LP values when all coefficients are sampled using a debiased construction valid under optimizer multiplicity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both selector endpoints are LP values with sampled objective coefficients and right-hand-side margins.

open_problems.open_problem: Exactly when can all margin-compatible micro-selectors in a lossy abstraction preserve one fixed canonical macro residual/intervention map, and when is realization possible only through selector-specific compatible residual projections?

source_refs.claim: Exact transformations require low- and high-level SEMs to agree on intervention predictions and emphasize that intervention maps must be specified explicitly.
source_refs.author: Paul K. Rubenstein, Sebastian Weichwald, Stephan Bongers, Joris M. Mooij, Dominik Janzing, Moritz Grosse-Wentrup, and Bernhard Schölkopf

source_refs.claim: The paper separates exact, uniform, abstraction, and strong-abstraction notions, showing that distribution-specific agreement is weaker than uniform structural agreement.
source_refs.author: Sander Beckers and Joseph Y. Halpern

source_refs.claim: COTA optimizes abstraction maps under causal constraints but does not characterize when a transportation polytope of selectors shares one canonical high-level residual map.
source_refs.author: Yorgos Felekis, Fabio Massimo Zennaro, Nicola Branchini, and Theodoros Damoulas
source_refs.venue: Conference on Causal Learning and Reasoning, PMLR 236

open_problems.why_unsolved: The abstraction hierarchy establishes that agreement produced by a favorable exogenous distribution need not imply uniform transformation, but it does not isolate selector coupling as the varying exogenous component. A free-selector construction may establish compatible macro responses separately for every gamma without preserving one predetermined residual map. The concrete unresolved object is the intersection of all selector-specific commutativity constraints; replacing the selector-specific existential quantifier by one common map would silently assert a stronger abstraction notion.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient structural characterization of when one fixed macro residual/intervention map commutes with every feasible selector coupling, accompanied by a smallest finite counterexample separating that class from the free-selector class.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation is organized around why successively stronger abstraction notions are needed and what each additional uniformity requirement excludes.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Distribution-specific agreement can conceal structural disagreement -> stronger abstractions require uniform intervention compatibility -> determine whether selector-envelope realizations satisfy a fixed-map notion or only a free-selector notion

method_exemplars.technique: Prove exact transformation through a commuting intervention diagram between structural models and use failed commutativity to construct counterexamples.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested boundary asks whether one intervention/residual map commutes for all micro-selector implementations.

method_exemplars.technique: Compare abstraction notions by changing the quantifier order over exogenous distributions, interventions, and low-to-high maps.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The free-versus-fixed selector distinction is a quantifier-order boundary of the same form.

open_problems.open_problem: For a PDX-derived precision-medicine rule deployed where tumor-profile frequencies and aggregate drug shares are observed but their joint allocation is unavailable, is superiority to a specified control uniform over every compatible selector, with a valid one-sided uncertainty statement?

source_refs.claim: The paper evaluates whether a precision-medicine assignment algorithm outperforms gold-standard, observed-treatment, and randomized-treatment controls using PDX outcomes.
source_refs.author: Jonas Béal and Aurélien Latouche

source_refs.claim: PDX studies expose heterogeneous responses across treatments and support individualized rules, but assume evaluable profile-specific allocations rather than deployment known only through marginal treatment shares.
source_refs.author: Naim U. Rashid et al.
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Manski shows that personalized medical decisions can be partially identified when outcome information and patient attributes are available at different aggregation levels.
source_refs.author: Charles F. Manski

source_refs.claim: Kallus and Zhou optimize worst-case policy regret over an uncertainty set and use the lower guarantee to prevent harmful deployment under unobserved confounding.
source_refs.author: Nathan Kallus and Angela Zhou

open_problems.why_unsolved: Béal–Latouche and Rashid et al. evaluate profile-specific treatment rules when the relevant joint rule or response surface is available. Manski treats ecological partial identification, while Kallus–Zhou protects policies against propensity-weight uncertainty. None supplies the sharp worst-case value of a fixed multi-drug deployment constrained simultaneously by target tumor-profile frequencies and exact aggregate drug shares. The missing allocation can reverse a control comparison whenever response heterogeneity aligns adversely with the unknown coupling.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp identified interval for the precision-strategy-minus-control value, a necessary-and-sufficient uniform-superiority criterion given by positivity of its lower endpoint, endpoint allocation certificates, and a simultaneous one-sided confidence procedure for that endpoint.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the destination estimand, PDX setting, and concrete control comparisons without suggesting that marginal-only deployment has been solved.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: PDX experiments reveal profile-by-drug response heterogeneity -> precision algorithms require comparison with clinically meaningful controls -> absent joint deployment logs, ask whether superiority survives every calibrated allocation

method_exemplars.technique: Formalize a personalized medical decision as an ecological-inference problem and derive conclusions valid across unobserved joint distributions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The PDX analysis likewise combines marginal evidence that does not reveal the joint profile-allocation law.

method_exemplars.technique: Define safe improvement through worst-case regret over a calibrated uncertainty set and optimize the lower policy guarantee.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Uniform superiority is a safe-improvement statement, with a transportation polytope replacing their propensity-ratio uncertainty set.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct an asymptotically efficient plug-in estimator for the value gain of an optimal constrained individualized rule relative to a reference rule.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a causal, control-relative inference template for constrained treatment allocation, although the selector endpoint is nonsmooth and partially identified.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the necessary-and-sufficient condition on the effective context-action support and response array mu(c,x) for every selector coupling with margins p and r to induce the same macro mean?

source_refs.claim: The paper gives substantive conditions under which multiple treatment versions may be ignored, but not a finite-support geometric criterion for invariance over all allocation couplings.
source_refs.author: Tyler J. VanderWeele and Miguel A. Hernán

source_refs.claim: Beckers and Halpern distinguish causal-abstraction notions according to how uniformly intervention predictions must agree.
source_refs.author: Sander Beckers and Joseph Y. Halpern

source_refs.claim: Optimal transport yields a sharp set under an unavailable joint law, but does not provide a selector-invariance criterion for causal abstractions.
source_refs.author: Xavier D'Haultfœuille, Christophe Gaillac, and Arnaud Maurel

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing multiple-version conditions are expressed through consistency, confounding, or stipulated version distributions, while causal-abstraction work classifies transformations through intervention commutativity. Neither yields a necessary-and-sufficient support-aware test for whether aggregate calibration eliminates selector ambiguity. Forced-zero edges are the obstacle: testing every formal 2-by-2 contrast is too strong on sparse support, while checking only observed rectangles can miss longer alternating cycles.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A point-identification theorem proving that the endpoint gap is zero exactly when every alternating-cycle contrast of mu vanishes on the effective bipartite support graph, equivalently when mu is a context potential plus an action potential on each relevant connected component.

writing_exemplar.why: Its central framing asks when versions alter the meaning of a treatment effect and when they may safely be ignored.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A coarse treatment contains outcome-relevant versions -> version allocation can alter the population effect -> characterize exactly when every calibrated allocation gives the same effect

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze constancy of a target functional over a coupling class using primal transport geometry and dual additive potentials.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired criterion is the dual-geometric condition for a cost to remain constant over a fixed-margin transportation polytope.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct pointwise inference for LP bounds that remains valid under point identification and multiple optimizer sets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An empirical analysis must distinguish a truly collapsed selector interval from sampling variation near a zero-width LP envelope.

literature_map:
1. VanderWeele and Hernán (2013, Journal of Causal Inference) show that effects of treatments with multiple versions depend on the version-assignment distribution and identify effects when that distribution is specified.
2. Béal and Latouche (2020, arXiv:2005.12427) formulate multiple-version precision-medicine effects and compare algorithms with gold-standard, observed-treatment, and randomized controls using PDX data.
3. Gao et al. (2015, Nature Medicine, DOI 10.1038/nm.3954) provide the high-throughput 1×1×1 PDX response substrate and document heterogeneous drug response across tumor models.
4. Rashid et al. (2021, JASA, DOI 10.1080/01621459.2020.1828091) learn high-dimensional individualized treatment rules from correlated multi-treatment PDX outcomes but do not address deployment observed only through separate margins.
5. Manski (2018, Quantitative Economics, DOI 10.3982/QE778) frames personalized medical decision-making with unlinked marginal information as ecological partial identification.
6. D'Haultfœuille, Gaillac, and Maurel (2025, ReStud, arXiv:2204.05175) use optimal transport for constructive sharp sets and inference when outcomes and covariates lie in datasets that cannot be linked.
7. Russell (2021, Journal of Business & Economic Statistics, DOI 10.1080/07350015.2019.1684300) and Ober-Reynolds (2023, arXiv:2311.09435) characterize sharp bounds on joint-potential-outcome functionals through transport, confirming the coupling geometry but not selector-abstraction semantics.
8. Gao, Ge, and Qian (2024, arXiv:2406.07868) formulate causal partial identification as multi-marginal optimal transport and derive rates for selected costs in a potential-outcomes setting.
9. Rubenstein et al. (2017, UAI, arXiv:1707.00819) introduce exact SEM transformations; Beckers and Halpern (2019, AAAI, arXiv:1812.03789) separate exact, uniform, abstraction, and strong-abstraction requirements.
10. Felekis et al. (2024, CLeaR, arXiv:2312.08107) combine causal constraints and multi-marginal transport to learn abstraction maps, the closest abstraction/transport paper but not a sharp selector-value-envelope result.
11. Fang and Santos (2019, ReStud) establish bootstrap failure and derivative-based resampling for directionally differentiable maps; Hong and Li (2018, Journal of Econometrics) supply the numerical-delta implementation.
12. Firpo, Galvao, and Parker (2023, Journal of Econometrics) treat inference for optimized value functions, while Voronin (2025, arXiv:2503.14940) directly handles LP bounds with all coefficients estimated and solution multiplicity through a debiased estimator.
13. Kallus and Zhou (2021, Management Science) formalize safe policy improvement by worst-case regret, and Qiu, Carone, and Luedtke (2022, arXiv:2201.06669) develop efficient inference for constrained individualized-rule values.
14. Fan, Park, and Xu (2026, Mathematics of Operations Research, arXiv:2307.00779) add Wasserstein uncertainty to marginal problems; Rischel and Weichwald (2021, UAI, arXiv:2103.15758) separately quantify compositional causal-abstraction error.
15. The central tension is that coupling-based sharpness, SCM abstraction compatibility, and nonsmooth joint inference exist in adjacent literatures, but the scan found no work unifying all three for calibrated selector noise with unobserved context-by-action deployment.
